knowledge_tree.title: PEP English Grade 4 Book 2
knowledge_tree.content: English textbook for Grade 4 students (second semester), covering topics like school, time, weather, farm, clothes, and shopping.

children.title: Unit 1: My School
children.content: Learning about school facilities and giving directions.

children.title: School Facilities Vocabulary
children.content: Words for different rooms and areas in a school.

children.title: teachers' office
children.content: A room where teachers work.

children.title: library
children.content: A place where books are kept for reading.

children.title: playground
children.content: An outdoor area for playing.

children.title: computer room
children.content: A room with computers for learning.

children.title: art room
children.content: A room for art classes.

children.title: music room
children.content: A room for music classes.

children.title: first floor
children.content: The ground level of a building.

children.title: second floor
children.content: The level above the first floor.

children.title: Preposition 'next to'
children.content: Used to describe something that is immediately adjacent to something else.

children.title: Asking for and Giving Directions
children.content: Phrases to ask where a place is and how to give simple directions.

children.title: Where's the ...?
children.content: Question used to ask for the location of something.

children.title: It's on the ... floor.
children.content: Phrase used to state which floor something is on.

children.title: Is this/that the ...?
children.content: Question to confirm the identity of a place.

children.title: Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.
children.content: Short answers to yes/no questions about identity.

children.title: Phonics: -er sound
children.content: Practicing the pronunciation of words ending with 'er'.

children.title: sister
children.content: A female sibling.

children.title: computer
children.content: An electronic device for processing data.

children.title: dinner
children.content: The main meal of the day.

children.title: winter
children.content: The coldest season of the year.

children.title: Unit 2: What Time Is It?
children.content: Learning to tell time and talk about daily routines.

children.title: Telling Time
children.content: Asking for and stating the time.

children.title: What time is it?
children.content: Question used to ask for the current time.

children.title: It's ... o'clock.
children.content: Phrase used to state the hour (e.g., It's 6 o'clock).

children.title: Daily Routines Vocabulary
children.content: Words and phrases for common daily activities.

children.title: get up
children.content: To rise from bed after sleeping.

children.title: go to school
children.content: To travel to the place of education.

children.title: go home
children.content: To return to one's house.

children.title: go to bed
children.content: To lie down in bed to sleep.

children.title: School Subjects
children.content: Names of different classes at school.

children.title: English class
children.content: A lesson where English is taught.

children.title: music class
children.content: A lesson where music is taught.

children.title: PE class
children.content: A lesson for physical education.

children.title: Meal Times
children.content: Words for different meals of the day.

children.title: breakfast
children.content: The first meal of the day.

children.title: lunch
children.content: A meal eaten in the middle of the day.

children.title: dinner
children.content: The main evening meal.

children.title: Expressing Time for an Activity
children.content: Using 'It's time for...' and 'It's time to...'.

children.title: It's time for + noun
children.content: Used to say it is the appropriate time for something (e.g., It's time for lunch).

children.title: It's time to + verb
children.content: Used to say it is the appropriate time to do something (e.g., It's time to go home).

children.title: Phonics: -ir, -ur sound
children.content: Practicing the pronunciation of words with 'ir' and 'ur'.

children.title: girl
children.content: A female child.

children.title: bird
children.content: A feathered animal that can fly.

children.title: nurse
children.content: A person trained to care for the sick.

children.title: hamburger
children.content: A cooked patty of ground meat, typically served in a bun.

children.title: Unit 3: Weather
children.content: Learning to describe different types of weather and temperatures.

children.title: Weather Adjectives
children.content: Words used to describe the weather.

children.title: cold
children.content: Having a low temperature.

children.title: warm
children.content: Having a moderately high temperature.

children.title: hot
children.content: Having a high temperature.

children.title: cool
children.content: Slightly cold, often in a pleasant way.

children.title: sunny
children.content: Bright with sunlight.

children.title: windy
children.content: With a lot of wind.

children.title: cloudy
children.content: Covered with clouds.

children.title: snowy
children.content: Characterized by falling snow.

children.title: rainy
children.content: Characterized by rainfall.

children.title: Asking About Weather
children.content: Question pattern to inquire about the weather in a place.

children.title: What's the weather like in ...?
children.content: Question used to ask about the weather conditions in a specific location.

children.title: Asking for Permission (Review/Extension)
children.content: Using 'Can I...?' to ask for permission to do something, often related to weather.

children.title: Can I go outside?
children.content: Asking for permission to go outdoors.

children.title: Yes, you can. / No, you can't.
children.content: Giving or denying permission.

children.title: Temperature in Degrees
children.content: Understanding and stating temperature using the term 'degrees'.

children.title: It's ... degrees.
children.content: Phrase used to state the temperature (e.g., It's 26 degrees).

children.title: Phonics: -ar, -al sound
children.content: Practicing the pronunciation of words with 'ar' and 'al'.

children.title: arm
children.content: The upper limb of the human body.

children.title: car
children.content: A road vehicle with an engine.

children.title: ball
children.content: A round object used in games.

children.title: tall
children.content: Of great height.

children.title: Unit 4: At the Farm
children.content: Learning vocabulary for farm animals and vegetables, and using demonstrative pronouns 'these' and 'those'.

children.title: Farm Vegetables Vocabulary
children.content: Names of common vegetables found on a farm.

children.title: tomato
children.content: A red or yellowish fruit with a juicy pulp, used as a vegetable.

children.title: potato
children.content: A starchy plant tuber that is a staple food.

children.title: green beans
children.content: The immature fruit of various kinds of bean plants, eaten as a vegetable.

children.title: carrot
children.content: A tapering orange-colored root eaten as a vegetable.

children.title: Farm Animals Vocabulary
children.content: Names of common animals found on a farm.

children.title: horse
children.content: A large plant-eating domesticated mammal with solid hoofs and a flowing mane and tail.

children.title: cow
children.content: A fully grown female animal of a domesticated breed of ox, kept to produce milk or beef.

children.title: sheep
children.content: A domesticated ruminant animal with a thick woolly coat.

children.title: hen
children.content: A female bird, especially of a domestic fowl.

children.title: Demonstrative Pronouns: these/those
children.content: Using 'these' for things near the speaker and 'those' for things farther away.

children.title: What are these?
children.content: Question about the identity of things near the speaker.

children.title: What are those?
children.content: Question about the identity of things away from the speaker.

children.title: They are ...
children.content: Answer to identify multiple things.

children.title: Are these ...? / Are those ...?
children.content: Yes/No questions to confirm the identity of multiple things.

children.title: Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
children.content: Short answers to yes/no questions about identity (plural).

children.title: Asking about Quantity
children.content: Using 'How many...?' to ask about the number of countable nouns.

children.title: How many ... do you have?
children.content: Question pattern to ask about the quantity of something someone possesses.

children.title: Phonics: -or, -world sound
children.content: Practicing the pronunciation of words with 'or' and the 'world' spelling.

children.title: horse
children.content: A large plant-eating domesticated mammal.

children.title: fork
children.content: An implement with prongs used for eating.

children.title: homework
children.content: Schoolwork assigned to be done outside the classroom.

children.title: world
children.content: The earth, together with all of its countries and peoples.

children.title: Unit 5: My Clothes
children.content: Learning vocabulary for clothing items and using possessive pronouns like 'yours', 'mine', and 'whose'.

children.title: Clothing Vocabulary
children.content: Words for common articles of clothing.

children.title: pants
children.content: A piece of clothing covering the body from the waist to the ankles.

children.title: hat
children.content: A shaped covering for the head worn for warmth, as a fashion item, or as part of a uniform.

children.title: dress
children.content: A one-piece garment for a woman or girl that covers the body and extends down over the legs.

children.title: skirt
children.content: A garment fastened around the waist and hanging down around the legs.

children.title: coat
children.content: An outer garment worn outdoors for warmth.

children.title: sweater
children.content: A knitted garment worn on the upper body to provide warmth.

children.title: socks
children.content: A piece of clothing worn on the feet and often under shoes.

children.title: shorts
children.content: A garment worn over the pelvic area, circling the waist and splitting to cover the upper part of the legs.

children.title: jacket
children.content: A short coat.

children.title: shirt
children.content: A cloth garment for the upper body.

children.title: Possessive Pronouns
children.content: Using pronouns like 'yours', 'mine' to show ownership.

children.title: yours
children.content: Belonging to or associated with the person or people that the speaker is addressing.

children.title: mine
children.content: Belonging to or associated with the speaker.

children.title: Asking about Ownership (Whose)
children.content: Using 'Whose...?' to ask which person something belongs to.

children.title: Whose ... is this?
children.content: Question to ask about the owner of a singular item.

children.title: Whose ... are these?
children.content: Question to ask about the owner of plural items.

children.title: It's ...'s.
children.content: Answer stating ownership using a name and apostrophe 's'.

children.title: They're ...'s.
children.content: Answer stating ownership for plural items using a name and apostrophe 's'.

children.title: Confirming Ownership (Are these yours?)
children.content: Asking yes/no questions to confirm if something belongs to someone.

children.title: Are these yours?
children.content: Question to confirm if plural items belong to the person being addressed.

children.title: Is this John's?
children.content: Question to confirm if a singular item belongs to a specific person (John).

children.title: Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
children.content: Short answers for plural ownership questions.

children.title: Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.
children.content: Short answers for singular ownership questions.

children.title: Phonics: -le sound
children.content: Practicing the pronunciation of words ending with 'le'.

children.title: apple
children.content: A round fruit with red, green, or yellow skin.

children.title: people
children.content: Human beings in general or considered collectively.

children.title: table
children.content: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.

children.title: Unit 6: Shopping
children.content: Learning language for shopping, including asking about prices and expressing opinions on items.

children.title: Shopping Items Vocabulary
children.content: Words for items commonly bought or sold.

children.title: gloves
children.content: A covering for the hand worn for protection against cold or dirt.

children.title: scarf
children.content: A length or square of fabric worn around the neck or head.

children.title: umbrella
children.content: A device consisting of a circular canopy on a folding metal frame supported by a central rod, used for protection against rain.

children.title: sunglasses
children.content: Glasses tinted to protect the eyes from sunlight or glare.

children.title: Adjectives for Description
children.content: Words used to describe items, especially in a shopping context.

children.title: pretty
children.content: Attractive in a delicate way.

children.title: expensive
children.content: Costing a lot of money.

children.title: cheap
children.content: Low in price.

children.title: nice
children.content: Pleasant; satisfactory.

children.title: Asking for Assistance
children.content: Phrase used to offer or request help in a store.

children.title: Can I help you?
children.content: Question asked by a shop assistant to a customer.

children.title: Asking to Try Things On
children.content: Requesting to put on clothing to check fit and appearance.

children.title: Can I try them on?
children.content: Asking for permission to put on items of clothing (plural, e.g., shoes).

children.title: Can I try it on?
children.content: Asking for permission to put on an item of clothing (singular, e.g., a dress).

children.title: Size ..., please.
children.content: Stating the desired size of a clothing item.

children.title: Expressing Fit/Opinion
children.content: Describing whether clothing fits or giving an opinion.

children.title: They're too big/small.
children.content: Stating that items of clothing are not the right size.

children.title: They're just right.
children.content: Stating that items of clothing fit perfectly.

children.title: How do you like this skirt?
children.content: Asking for someone's opinion on an item.

children.title: It's very pretty.
children.content: Giving a positive opinion on an item's appearance.

children.title: Asking About Price
children.content: Question pattern to ask how much something costs.

children.title: How much is this/that ...?
children.content: Question to ask the price of a singular item.

children.title: How much are these/those ...?
children.content: Question to ask the price of plural items.

children.title: It's ... yuan/dollars.
children.content: Stating the price of a singular item.

children.title: They're ... yuan/dollars.
children.content: Stating the price of plural items.

children.title: Phonics: Review of various sounds
children.content: Reviewing previously learned phonics patterns.

triplets.head: Confirming Ownership
triplets.relation: uses question pattern for singular specific
